what_this_is: The paraphrase / near-miss set for the semantic cache threshold sweep (D-041, G-03). Committed rather than living in an ad-hoc script, because the 2C recalibration was run from one and could not be re-run against a different embedder without rewriting it.
how_to_read_it: `paraphrases` mean the same question and MUST hit the cache. `near_misses` are lexically close and semantically different, and MUST NOT — a false hit is not a cheaper answer, it is a wrong answer delivered fluently, cited, and about the right part. False hits are therefore binding and absolute; hit rate is only cost.
why_these_pairs: Every pair is grounded in the golden chapter, so the same corpus drives the cache sweep, the floor sweep and the faithfulness harness. The near-misses are built to be hard for a LEXICAL embedder and for a SEMANTIC one in different ways: some share almost every content word while asking a different question (nm01, nm03), and some share few words while being genuinely about the same thing — which is where a lexical embedder fails and a semantic one should not. That asymmetry is the point of running this on both.

paraphrases.probe: What is the function of the pupil?
paraphrases.note: Near-identical wording. If this misses, the threshold is unusable at any setting.

paraphrases.seeded: Where is visual acuity greatest in the retina?
paraphrases.probe: Which part of the retina gives the sharpest vision?
paraphrases.note: Same question, almost no shared content words. This is the one a lexical embedder should fail and a semantic one should pass.

paraphrases.seeded: What fluid fills the posterior cavity of the eye?
paraphrases.probe: What is the space behind the lens filled with?
paraphrases.note: Same question by description rather than by name.

paraphrases.probe: Which photosensitive pigment is found in rod photoreceptors?

paraphrases.seeded: What are the three layers of the eye?
paraphrases.probe: Name the three tunics of the eyeball.
paraphrases.note: Same question in the technical register the chapter uses.

near_misses.note: Two content words apart, and a different part. The cache is scoped per part, so this also has to be wrong ACROSS scopes to be a real test.

near_misses.seeded: What fluid fills the posterior cavity of the eye?
near_misses.probe: What fluid fills the anterior cavity of the eye?
near_misses.note: One word apart, opposite answer. Aqueous and vitreous humor are different fluids in different chambers.
One word apart. The chapter answers the first specifically (rhodopsin) and the second only generically.

near_misses.seeded: Where is visual acuity greatest in the retina?
near_misses.probe: Where is visual acuity worst in the retina?
near_misses.note: A single antonym. Any embedder that treats negation as noise hits here, and a student gets the opposite of the truth.

near_misses.seeded: What are the three layers of the eye?
near_misses.probe: What are the three layers of the retina?
near_misses.note: Same shape, different structure. The chapter answers one and not the other.
Both vascular-tunic vocabulary, unrelated questions. The easy negative, kept as a floor: a threshold that hits here is broken outright.
